questions.subject: English
questions.stem: Your school is holding an assembly on the girl child. Write a speech of about 100 words on why every girl should be sent to school. Address the students directly and end with a formal closing.

markingPoints.description: Content: gives at least two sound reasons why girls should be sent to school.
Format: speech opens with a greeting and closes with a formal remark of thanks.
Organisation: points are arranged in a clear order and end in a call to the audience.
Accuracy: correct grammar, spelling and punctuation.
Expression: earnest tone and vocabulary suited to a school assembly.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: Good morning everyone. Every morning, in our own villages, some little girl sits at home while her brothers go to school. Nobody stops her, and nobody is blamed. But the moment she learns to read, she learns to speak, to think and to choose her own life. A family that keeps a daughter at home loses not only her learning but her voice. We must send every girl to school, we must keep her there, and we must never laugh at the way she speaks. Thank you.

questions.stem: A girl in your class stammers, so she is afraid to answer aloud and her family now says she is not fit to study. Write an e-mail of about 100 words to your teacher describing her fear and suggesting that she be allowed to answer aloud in class. Begin with 'Dear Ma'am' and end with 'Regards' followed by your name.

markingPoints.description: Content: describes the pupil's fear and the family's attitude, then makes the two clear requests.
Format: e-mail opens with 'Dear Ma'am' and closes with 'Regards' and the writer's name.
Organisation: description comes first, request follows, and the whole is kept brief.
Accuracy: correct grammar, spelling and punctuation.
Expression: polite, sympathetic and direct wording.

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
Dear Ma'am

Our class has a pupil who stammers. At home she is called the simpleton and her family now says that she is not fit to study. Because of this she is afraid to answer aloud in class and keeps her head down. I request you to let her answer aloud in class every day and to praise her each time she manages to speak. Please also give her a book with pictures and big print, as a book like that gives a pupil the courage to try. I am sure she will improve.

Regards
Aarti Sharma

questions.stem: Why did Ramlal's wife decide that only Bholi should be sent to school? Answer in about 50 words.

markingPoints.description: She believed Bholi had little chance of getting married because of her ugly face and lack of sense.
Sending Bholi alone would please the Tehsildar without risking the other daughters' marriages.
She expected the teachers at school to bear the responsibility for Bholi.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: Ramlal's wife knew that no bridegroom would come for Bholi because of her ugly, pock-marked face and her lack of sense. Sending Bholi alone would please the Tehsildar without risking the marriage of her other daughters. She also felt that the teachers at school, not her family, should shoulder the care of her.

questions.stem: How did the way the teacher spoke to Bholi change the course of her life? Answer in about 50 words.

markingPoints.description: She spoke softly and treated Bholi kindly instead of ordering or mocking her.
She praised every attempt at Bholi's name and promised her a book, and then a bigger one.
Bholi took courage, went home happy and returned to school early the next morning.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: The teacher never ordered or mocked Bholi. She spoke in a soft, soothing voice, asked her to get up as a friendly suggestion, praised every attempt at her name and promised her one book and then a bigger one. Bholi, who had always been laughed at, began to hope, went home happy and came back early the next morning.

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: Show in steps, in about 120 words, why a family agreed to hand its daughter to a bridegroom it did not respect, and what made her refuse him at the altar.

markingPoints.description: He was a well-to-do grocer with a big shop, a house of his own and several thousand in the bank, and asked for no dowry.
They argued that forty-five or fifty is no great age for a man.
He came from another village and did not know about her pock-marks and her lack of sense.
Ramlal feared she might remain unmarried all her life if the proposal was refused.
Ramlal placed his turban, his honour, at the bridegroom's feet to save the family's izzat.
She flung the garland into the fire and refused, calling him a mean, greedy and contemptible coward.

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
1. Her parents were told that Bishamber Nath was a well-to-do grocer with a big shop, a house of his own and several thousand in the bank, and he asked for no dowry.
2. They told themselves that forty-five or fifty is no great age for a man, and only shrugged at his limp.
3. He came from another village and did not know about her pock-marks and her lack of sense.
4. Ramlal feared that if he refused, Bholi would remain unmarried all her life, and he feared for the family's izzat.
5. So Bholi was dressed as a bride, though she called him a mean, greedy and contemptible coward.
6. When he demanded five thousand rupees after his turban had been placed at his feet, she flung the garland into the fire and said she would not marry him.

questions.stem: Show in steps, in about 120 words, the contrast between how one family treated its youngest daughter in her childhood and the place she claimed for herself afterwards.

markingPoints.description: She was neglected though the household was prosperous, with plenty to eat and drink.
New clothes had never been made for her and she wore the old dresses of her sisters.
Her parents worried only because she had neither good looks nor intelligence and might remain unmarried.
Her mother chose to send her alone to school and left the teachers to worry about her.
Her teacher gave her a book and promised a bigger one each month, so she returned every day.
After refusing the marriage she calmly promised to serve her parents and teach in that same school.

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
1. She was neglected at home, though the family was a prosperous farmer's household with plenty to eat and drink.
2. New clothes had never been made for her; she wore her sisters' old dresses, and no one mended or washed them.
3. Her parents worried about her only because she had neither good looks nor intelligence and might never be married.
4. Her mother decided to send just her to school, expecting the teachers there to worry about her.
5. Her teacher gave her a book with big letters and promised a bigger book each month, and she came back every day.
6. Years later, after refusing a greedy match, she calmly promised to serve her parents and to teach in that same school.
